data.title: Cardiff Lexington Creates New A-1 Preferred Control Shares
data.description:
Cardiff Lexington ( (CDIX) ) has issued an update.

On August 31, 2026, Cardiff Lexington Corporation filed a certificate of designation in Nevada creating a new series A-1 preferred stock, limited to two shares and structured to rank senior to common stock, on parity with series A preferred, and junior to several existing senior preferred series. The A-1 shares carry a $250 stated value in liquidation, have no dividend or economic participation rights, and are entitled to a voting power equal to 25% of all other equity votes plus one, though they convert automatically into common stock upon most transfers, effectively concentrating control while minimally affecting the company’s economic capitalization.

This move formalizes an instrument designed primarily for voting control rather than financial return, potentially influencing corporate governance dynamics and decision-making without materially diluting common shareholders’ economic interests. By separating economic rights from voting power and tightly limiting transferability, Cardiff Lexington reinforces a capital structure that can stabilize control among designated holders while preserving existing priority arrangements among senior and parity securities in the event of corporate transactions or liquidation.

data.title: Novartis Pelacarsen Fails to Cut Cardiovascular Events in Key Phase III Lp(a) Trial
data.description:
Novartis ( (NVS) ) has provided an announcement.

On September 4, 2026, Novartis reported topline Phase III results from its Lp(a)HORIZON trial evaluating pelacarsen in 8,323 patients with elevated lipoprotein(a) and established cardiovascular disease. The study, a major outcomes trial, did not meet its primary endpoint, as lowering Lp(a) with pelacarsen failed to significantly reduce a composite of cardiovascular death, non‑fatal myocardial infarction, non‑fatal stroke and urgent coronary revascularization versus placebo.

Pelacarsen, an investigational antisense oligonucleotide licensed from Ionis Pharmaceuticals, did achieve substantial Lp(a) reductions in patients already receiving guideline‑directed lipid‑lowering and antihypertensive therapy. However, the lack of demonstrated event‑risk reduction in this optimized‑care population challenges expectations for Lp(a)‑targeted drugs and may influence future development strategies, while still offering valuable scientific insight into the complex link between genetic Lp(a) elevation and cardiovascular outcomes.

data.description:
ONEX Corporation ((TSE:ONEX)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

ONEX Corporation’s latest earnings call struck a cautiously upbeat tone, with management highlighting strong operational progress at Convex, improving balance sheet metrics, and growing fee-generating assets under management. While mark-to-market losses, softer insurance pricing, and fundraising execution risks weighed on reported results, the message to investors was that the structural trajectory of earnings and capital return remains favorable.

Convex Delivers Premium Growth and Superior Underwriting

Convex was the clear bright spot, with gross premiums written reaching $1.9 billion in Q2, up 8% year over year. The unit posted net income of $169 million, a combined ratio of 85% for the quarter, and an improved 84% combined ratio over the last 12 months, driving a 38% jump in adjusted net income to $719 million and return on average tangible equity of 20.3%.

It now represents 44% of ONEX’s investing capital, with the valuation anchored on a 2x price-to-tangible-book multiple that implies a roughly 9.8x price-to-earnings ratio on last-12-month adjusted net income.

Repositioning Capital and Strengthening the Balance Sheet

Management emphasized a sharp shift in the mix of investing capital, with private equity’s share falling from $5.6 billion, or 65%, to $4.4 billion, or 46%, in just six months. The NAV loan used to fund the Convex deal was cut from $700 million to $220 million, leaving ONEX in a net neutral cash position and lifting investing capital per share to $123.99, up 6% over 12 months.

Realizations Boost DPI and Support Future Fundraising

ONEX generated approximately $1.4 billion of distributions from Onex Partners over the past year, excluding Convex. Onex Partners V has now reached a 1.0x distributed-to-paid-in multiple, and expected realizations from ONCAP Fund IV should push that vehicle’s DPI above 1.0, which management believes will be a key support for raising Onex Partners VI.

Credit Platform Scales Fee-Generating AUM and Structured Credit FRE

Fee-generating assets under management climbed to $43.2 billion at quarter end, up 6% year over year, driven by strong credit growth. Credit FGAUM reached $30.6 billion, up about 13% over the last 12 months, while structured credit strategies delivered $19 million in fee-related earnings in Q2, marking their best quarter yet.

Progress Toward Asset Management FRE Ambitions

Run-rate management fees stood at $211 million as ONEX works toward a $35 million exit run-rate in fee-related earnings by 2026. Management made clear that hitting this target is contingent on a successful first close for Onex Partners VI later this year, with AIG’s $2 billion commitment already in deployment and expected to underpin future FRE growth.

Liquidity Strength Enables Buyback Resumption

The company reported $287 million of cash and near-cash and $600 million of undrawn revolving credit capacity, along with unfunded commitments reduced to $275 million. With the NAV loan down to $220 million, ONEX signaled that it will immediately resume share repurchases and still retain ample liquidity to pursue accretive strategic investments.

Mark-to-Market Losses Weigh on Investment Returns

Despite strong underwriting, Convex’s net investment returns were $45 million lower than a year ago, mainly due to mark-to-market losses in fixed-income holdings. Year-to-date, Convex recorded $62 million of such losses, prompting management to shift fixed income to an available-for-sale classification so future unrealized swings will sit outside net income.

Insurance Pricing Headwinds in Short-Tail Lines

The call flagged a softer pricing backdrop in parts of the insurance market, particularly short-tail classes like property. Year-to-date rate changes were around negative 5%, forcing Convex to rely on selective underwriting and disciplined risk selection rather than pure price increases to sustain its top-line and profitability.

Selective Private Equity Markdowns Damp Quarterly Results

Private equity investing capital produced a modest 4% return over the last 12 months but was flat in the quarter as several positions were marked down. Management cited slight quarterly declines in Onex Partners and ONCAP valuations, driven by public comparables and valuation reassessments, underscoring a more cautious stance on PE marks.

Credit Capital Hit by Market Volatility and CLO Marks

ONEX’s credit investing capital posted a 2% loss over the last 12 months and a sub-1% loss in the quarter, reflecting broader credit market volatility. Unrealized mark-to-market declines in European CLOs and opportunistic credit strategies weighed on performance, even as the firm continued to grow credit AUM and fee streams.

Low In-Quarter FRE Highlights Fundraising Sensitivity

Fee-related earnings for the quarter were just $4 million, underscoring how dependent ONEX’s near-term earnings are on fundraising, transaction timing, and market conditions. Management acknowledged that moving from this low base to the targeted FRE run-rate will require successful execution on upcoming fund closes and continuation vehicles.

Fundraising Execution Remains a Key Strategic Risk

The path to $35 million of exit run-rate FRE by 2026 rests heavily on a first close for Onex Partners VI in the fourth quarter. Management stressed that capital allocation plans, earnings visibility, and some expansion initiatives are tied to this fundraising milestone, making execution risk a central consideration for investors.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Strategic Trajectory

Looking ahead, ONEX reiterated its confidence in reaching $35 million of exit run-rate FRE by the end of 2026, assuming timely success with Onex Partners VI. The company plans to resume share buybacks immediately, backed by stronger liquidity and a leaner NAV loan, while continuing to leverage Convex’s underwriting strength and expanding credit AUM to drive earnings and capital growth.

ONEX’s earnings call showcased a business increasingly anchored by Convex’s robust performance and a more balanced investing capital mix, even as market volatility and fundraising timing created near-term noise. For investors, the key takeaway is that the firm is moving toward higher recurring fee income and renewed share repurchases, with execution on Onex Partners VI likely to be the main swing factor for the stock over the next year.
